seed: Shannon Byrne Susko, System by System post Hedgehog and BHAG and worksheet Hedgehog Concept and BHAG Validation; Jim Collins, Good to Great; Byron Darlison, Why Does Your Company Exist?

slides.title: Your BHAG sits where three circles meet.
slides.support: Agree each circle in turn. The BHAG comes last.

artwork.alt: Three overlapping circles, Core Purpose, Core Business and Economic Engine, each with its question, and the BHAG where all three meet: a 10 to 30 year goal with no numbers.

notes: This is Jim Collins’s Hedgehog Concept. The BHAG sits where three things meet: why the company exists, what its core business is, and how it makes money.
The BHAG the team gutted out at the Kick Off was good enough to build execution momentum. A year on, the team has the confidence for a full discussion about it.
The Hedgehog is about focus, not fantasy.
The Core Purpose the team just confirmed goes in the top circle. Then work through the other two circles in order.
slides.headline: Your BHAG sits where three circles meet.

slides.title: What is your core business?
slides.support: Each leader writes an answer alone. Then share.
body: It is what you can be best in the world at, not what you want to be best at.
Which answer says it most clearly? Stay with it until the team agrees.
It describes the company today. Your 3HAG statement describes what it will become.
notes: Many leadership teams find it hard to say what business they are in. Give it time.

Each leader writes an answer and all share. Ask which one says it most clearly, then wait. Once one leader makes a stand, the others agree or disagree. Keep the discussion going until the team agrees.
Best in the world means real capability, not ambition.
slides.headline: What is your core business?

slides.title: What is your Profit per X?
slides.support: Your economic engine. X is a widget from your KFFM.
body: If you have agreed your X, read it aloud and confirm it.
If not, each leader writes an answer. Share, then agree.
notes: Profit per X is the one unit that drives the economics of the core business.
Look at the KFFM. X is a widget from the map. Profit per employee is not the X unless the company’s business is placing people.
On the first pass Profit per X was a hypothesis. A year of running the KFFM is how the team has tested it.
slides.headline: What is your Profit per X?

slides.title: What is your 10 to 30 year goal?
slides.support: Each leader writes it alone. No numbers. Then share.
body: Stay with it until the team agrees.
You leave with a new BHAG, or the same BHAG well tested.
notes: Only start this step when the team agrees on all three circles.
Each leader writes what they think the company’s 10 to 30 year goal is, and all share. Ask which one is the BHAG, then wait for a leader to make a stand.
The outcome is a new BHAG or a well-validated one. Either is a good result.
slides.headline: What is your 10 to 30 year goal?
